windows.reason: ROCm/HIP port validated on windows-gfx1151 (physical AMD Radeon 8060S, hardware AMD OpenGL ICD confirmed via GL_RENDERER, not software GL). All HIP compute passes: gpu_mat_test 4/4, GPU SIFT matching 31/31, opengl_utils_test 3/3, 1530 assertions total. The sole GPU-test failure is ExtractSiftFeaturesGPU.Nominal, which heap-corrupts (STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION 0xc0000374) in SiftGPU PyramidCU destructor -> glDeleteBuffers during PBO teardown. Root cause is a pre-existing upstream COLMAP Windows bug in UNMODIFIED code: OpenGLContextManager::MakeCurrent (src/colmap/util/opengl_utils.cc:80-86) makes the GL context current on a temporary std::thread then joins it, leaving the context owned by a dead thread; the destructor later calls glDeleteBuffers with no current context. The port does not touch opengl_utils.cc or PyramidCU.cpp (git diff main..moat-port is empty for both). On Linux the AMD Mesa driver tolerates this cross-thread GL teardown; the strict Windows AMD ICD does not. Upstream GL-context-lifecycle defect exposed by (not caused by) enabling GPU SIFT on AMD; not a portability defect in the HIP port.
